title: Cut Into the Most Different Pieces
statement: Cut `text` into **non-empty pieces** (together they give back the whole text, in order) so that **no two pieces are equal**. Return the **largest number of pieces** you can get. An empty text has `0` pieces.

examples.explanation: a | ab | b | aa. Five different pieces would need four single letters or similar, but there are only two different letters.

hints.nudge: Decide where the first piece ends, then solve the same problem for the rest, remembering which pieces are already used. When can a branch be abandoned early?
hints.pattern: Backtracking over the cut positions with a set of the pieces used so far; prune a branch when the pieces so far plus the number of letters left cannot beat the best result.
hints.pseudocode:
go(start, count): if count + (n - start) <= best: return   (even single letters could not beat it)
  if start == n: best = max(best, count); return
  for end in start + 1 .. n: piece = text[start..end); if piece not in used: add it; go(end, count + 1); remove it
hints.walkthrough: There are 2^(n-1) ways to cut a text of n letters; for n = 16 that is 32,768 cuttings: small enough to try all of them with a set to detect repeated pieces. The search is a depth-first backtracking: choose the end of the next piece, skip it if the same piece was used before, recurse, and remove the piece again when you return. A simple pruning rule speeds it up: even if all remaining letters became single-letter pieces you could only add (n - start) more pieces, so if count + (n - start) is not larger than the best found so far the branch cannot improve the answer.
